rulers.name: Li Gui
rulers.title: Great Prince of Liang west of the River (fall 617); emperor of Liang (November 618)
rulers.note: Infobox reign 14 August 617 to 29 June 619; era Anle from 26 November 618.

correction.text: Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping (Xining) and Fuhan (Linxia): the land west of the Yellow River

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page names Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping and Fuhan and puts the Yellow River as the western boundary of his territory; Jincheng (Lanzhou) was Xue Ju's. The Hexi Corridor with circles at Xining and Linxia is the researcher's reading; the page gives no area. The Tang dossier draws the same land as a 619 gain.

ledger.note: 617: Li Gui rises at Wuwei. In summer 617 he and his associates decide 'to rise against Sui rule at Wuwei'; in the fall he claims the title 'Great Prince of Liang west of the River' (infobox reign from 14 August 617).

region.text: Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping (Xining) and Fuhan (Linxia): the land west of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 617: the Hexi towns join. After the fall 617 rising, 'Li Gui soon took four other commanderies' (Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping and Fuhan), controlling the land west of the Yellow River; he also destroys the Western Tujue general Ashina Kandu who had submitted and then rebelled. The page gives no season; the month is a sort key after the August 617 rising (reviewer ea-04-x: the year was 618, which the page does not support).
618: Li Gui declares himself emperor of Liang. In the winter of 618 (era Anle from 26 November 618) he names his son Li Boyu crown prince, before Tang's envoy Zhang Qide arrives.

region.text: Wuwei, Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping (Xining) and Fuhan (Linxia): the land west of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 619: An Xinggui captures Li Gui. In spring 619 Li Gui sends Deng Xiao to submit; Gaozu has the Tuyuhun under Murong Fuyun attack Liang; in summer (infobox 29 June 619) the Tang official An Xinggui 'enters Wuwei, raises the Xiongnu chiefs against Li Gui, and captures him'. Gaozu executes Li Gui and his sons and brothers.

wars.name: Tang-Tuyuhun campaign against Li Gui
wars.outcome: Tang arranged a Tuyuhun attack in spring 619 and An Xinggui's coup captured Li Gui at Wuwei in June 619; the Liang was handed to the Tang.
wars.note: Not a Wikipedia article title; named from the page's account.

certainty.note: Rebel state with no frontier on the page except the Yellow River on the east.

sources.title: Li Gui (warlord)
sources.note: Rise at Wuwei summer 617, the towns taken 617-618, the November 618 imperial title, 619 submission and capture, infobox dates.

notes: Written for ea-04-x (a rebel state of the Sui-Tang transition that ea-04-a, the Tang dossier, lists as 'Li Gui (Liang of Hexi)'; no Cliopatria row). The Tang dossier has the 619 gain and no 617-618 loss events (the Sui dossier has none either); the Tang page's text names no place, so the Hexi Corridor is the researcher's reading, here refined with Xining and Linxia from the Li Gui page. Western Tujue (Ashina Kandu) and Tuyuhun appear only in the war. The Li Gui disambiguation page was opened (and Li_Gui_(Liang) failed) before the right article was found.
